key_insight: The paper shows that neural network calibration can be learned jointly with classification in one training loop, removing the need for a separate post-hoc calibration step.
engineering_relevance: This simplifies deployment by improving calibration without extra calibration data, extra model-selection overhead, or added parameter cost in the final layer-based setup.
method: Formulate calibration as a bilevel Stackelberg optimization problem trained end-to-end with the backbone.
Use standard cross-entropy to jointly optimize accuracy and calibration, with the calibrator learning rate as the only extra hyperparameter.
Test calibrators ranging from temperature/matrix scaling to neural layers, with the final classification layer used as a zero-extra-parameter calibrator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art calibrators while keeping complexity minimal and avoiding separate calibration sets.
watch_item: Performance may depend on tuning the calibrator learning rate, and more flexible calibrators could still add overhead in multi-task or larger systems.
paper_title: Calibration in One Go: Jointly Learning Accurate and Calibrated Neural Networks
